questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Pocked with rust after decades outdoors, [[the conservator inspected the iron gate]].
choices: NO CHANGE
an inspection revealed the iron gate needed treatment
there was damage to the iron gate
the iron gate needed careful treatment
questions.explanation: Pocked with rust describes the iron gate, so gate must be the subject after the opening description. The keyed choice supplies that subject. A conservator, an inspection, and there do not name the rusty object being described.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Walking through the gallery, [[Elena admired the paintings]].
choices: NO CHANGE
it amazed Elena to see the paintings
the paintings amazed Elena
the paintings were admired by Elena
questions.explanation: 'Walking through the gallery' modifies the person walking, so 'Elena' must follow the comma, and the original is correct. The other choices put 'the paintings' or 'it' right after the comma, none of which can walk, so each dangles the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Ripe and bright red, [[Jordan picked the strawberries from the garden]].
choices: NO CHANGE
Jordan filled a basket with strawberries
picking went quickly that morning
the strawberries were ready to be picked
questions.explanation: 'Ripe and bright red' describes the strawberries, so 'the strawberries' must follow the comma. 'Jordan' and the gerund 'picking' cannot be ripe and bright red, so 'Jordan picked the strawberries from the garden,' 'Jordan filled a basket with strawberries,' and 'picking went quickly that morning' all dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Smiling at the camera, [[the portrait captured the bride perfectly]].
choices: NO CHANGE
the bride posed for the portrait
the camera flash lit the studio
a flawless portrait resulted
questions.explanation: 'Smiling at the camera' describes the bride, so 'the bride' must follow the comma; a portrait, a camera flash, and an abstract result cannot smile, which dangles the modifier in the other choices.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Thrilled by the final score, [[the fans let out a loud cheer]].
choices: NO CHANGE
there was a loud cheer from the fans
the loud cheer echoed for the fans
a loud cheer was let out by the fans
questions.explanation: 'Thrilled by the final score' describes the fans, so 'the fans' must follow the comma, and the original is correct. The other choices put 'a loud cheer,' 'the loud cheer,' or 'there' after the comma, none of which can feel thrilled, so each dangles the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Having been collected at three different depths, [[the technician compared the water samples]].
choices: NO CHANGE
there were differences among the water samples
a comparison of the water samples was made
the water samples were compared by the technician
questions.explanation: The water samples were collected at different depths, so they must be the subject of the main clause. The passive keyed choice correctly keeps samples as that subject. The original attaches the opener to the technician, and the other choices make there or a comparison the subject rather than the collected material.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: To win the science fair, [[a working volcano was built by Priya]].
choices: NO CHANGE
Priya built a working volcano
the judges praised Priya's volcano
the gymnasium hosted the event
questions.explanation: The infinitive opener 'To win the science fair' must describe whoever wants to win, so 'Priya' must follow the comma; a volcano, the judges, and the gymnasium are not trying to win, so those choices dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Running to catch the bus, [[I felt my backpack slip off my shoulder]].
choices: NO CHANGE
my backpack slipped off my shoulder
my shoulder dropped the backpack
the backpack on my shoulder slipped
questions.explanation: 'Running to catch the bus' must describe a person, so 'I' must follow the comma, and the original is correct. The other choices put 'my backpack' or 'my shoulder' after the comma, neither of which can run, so each dangles the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Eager to begin the experiment, [[the equipment was set up quickly by the students]].
choices: NO CHANGE
the students set up the equipment quickly
setup of the equipment went quickly
the experiment got under way quickly
questions.explanation: 'Eager to begin the experiment' describes the people who are eager, so 'the students' must follow the comma; equipment, setup, and an experiment cannot feel eager, so those choices dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Hidden beneath the floorboards for decades, [[the new owners discovered a box of gold coins]].
choices: NO CHANGE
a box of gold coins surprised the new owners
the discovery thrilled everyone
the curious owners pried up a loose board
questions.explanation: 'Hidden beneath the floorboards for decades' describes the box, so 'a box of gold coins' must follow the comma. The new owners, the curious owners, and 'the discovery' were not hidden under the floor, so those choices dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice most clearly states that the beam was on the eastern wall and the laser was the measuring tool?
questions.stem: The technician measured the beam [[with a laser on the eastern wall]].
choices: NO CHANGE
with a laser that was on the eastern wall
on the eastern wall using a laser
using the eastern wall with a laser
questions.explanation: On the eastern wall must identify the beam’s location, while using a laser states the measuring tool. The keyed wording separates those roles. The original and the next choice locate the laser on the wall; the final choice makes the wall itself something used for measuring rather than clearly locating the beam.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: A loyal companion for twelve years, [[the family was heartbroken when the dog died]].
choices: NO CHANGE
the family grieved for weeks afterward
the dog left the family heartbroken when it died
the dog's death devastated everyone
questions.explanation: 'A loyal companion for twelve years' describes the dog, so 'the dog' must be the subject right after the comma. 'The family was heartbroken,' 'the family grieved,' and 'the dog's death devastated everyone' each put something other than the companion there, dangling the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice most clearly expresses that the writer watched almost all of the series?
questions.stem: I [[nearly watched the entire series]] over winter break, stopping just two episodes short of the finale.
choices: NO CHANGE
watched the entire series nearly
watched nearly the entire series
the entire series nearly watched
questions.explanation: 'Watched nearly the entire series' puts the limiter directly beside the amount watched and matches the two unwatched episodes. 'Nearly watched' can be ambiguous about whether the viewing happened at all. The other two placements are unidiomatic in this sentence.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Designed by a celebrated architect, [[the bridge draws photographers from around the world]].
choices: NO CHANGE
tourists photograph the bridge constantly
photographs of the bridge appear everywhere
tourists with cameras gather at the bridge
questions.explanation: 'Designed by a celebrated architect' must modify the thing designed, the bridge, so 'the bridge' must follow the comma, and the original is correct. The other choices put 'tourists' or 'photographs' after the comma, none of which were designed by the architect, so each dangles the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice most clearly indicates that the professor spent decades developing the theory?
questions.stem: The professor explained [[the theory to her students that she had spent decades developing]].
choices: NO CHANGE
to her students the theory that she had spent decades developing
the theory to her students that they had developed
the theory to her students, who had spent decades developing it
questions.explanation: 'To her students the theory that she had spent decades developing' places the relative clause immediately after its intended antecedent, theory. The original separates the clause from theory with students; the remaining choices explicitly credit students with the development.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: To qualify for the scholarship, [[a portfolio of essays must be submitted by each applicant]].
choices: NO CHANGE
each applicant must submit a portfolio of essays
a portfolio of essays is required for the scholarship
the committee reviews each applicant's portfolio
questions.explanation: The infinitive opener 'To qualify for the scholarship' must describe whoever qualifies, so 'each applicant' must follow the comma; a portfolio and the committee are not the ones qualifying, so those choices dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Frozen solid overnight, [[Marcus scraped the windshield before driving]].
choices: NO CHANGE
the windshield needed scraping before Marcus could drive
driving required some scraping first
Marcus had to scrape before driving
questions.explanation: 'Frozen solid overnight' describes the windshield, so 'the windshield' must follow the comma. 'Marcus scraped the windshield' makes Marcus the frozen thing, while 'Marcus had to scrape' and 'driving required some scraping' leave nothing frozen at all, dangling the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Buzzing loudly around the porch light, [[Nadia swatted at the moths]].
choices: NO CHANGE
swatting did little to stop them
the moths circled while Nadia swatted at them
Nadia waved her arms at them
questions.explanation: 'Buzzing loudly around the porch light' describes the moths, so 'the moths' must follow the comma. 'Nadia swatted at the moths' and 'Nadia waved her arms' make Nadia the one buzzing, and 'swatting did little to stop them' supplies no buzzing noun, dangling the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Stacked neatly on the counter, [[the baker boxed the warm muffins]].
choices: NO CHANGE
the baker reached for the warm muffins
the warm muffins waited to be boxed
boxing the warm muffins took a while
questions.explanation: 'Stacked neatly on the counter' describes the muffins, so 'the warm muffins' must follow the comma. 'The baker boxed the warm muffins' puts the baker on the counter, while 'the baker reached for the warm muffins' and 'boxing the warm muffins took a while' dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Soaked from the sudden downpour, [[the hikers wrung out their jackets]].
choices: NO CHANGE
the storm showed no sign of easing
the downpour drenched everything
wringing out the jackets helped a little
questions.explanation: 'Soaked from the sudden downpour' describes the hikers, and the original already places 'the hikers' right after the comma. 'The storm,' 'the downpour,' and the gerund 'wringing' cannot be soaked by the rain, so those choices dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: The vendor sold balloons [[to the children filled with helium]].
choices: NO CHANGE
filled with helium to the children
to the children, who were filled with helium
to the helium-filled children
questions.explanation: 'Filled with helium' describes the balloons, so it must sit beside 'balloons,' giving 'balloons filled with helium to the children.' 'To the children filled with helium,' 'to the children, who were filled with helium,' and 'to the helium-filled children' all claim the children were full of helium.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: After studying the migration data for months, [[the biologist noticed surprising patterns]].
choices: NO CHANGE
surprising patterns emerged for the biologist
surprising patterns became clear
there were surprising patterns to report
questions.explanation: 'After studying the migration data for months' describes whoever studied, so 'the biologist' must follow the comma, and the original is correct. The other choices put 'surprising patterns' or 'there' after the comma, none of which can study data, so each dangles the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: To avoid the rush-hour traffic, [[an earlier train was taken by Lena]].
choices: NO CHANGE
Lena took an earlier train
the earlier train seemed wiser
an earlier departure made sense
questions.explanation: The infinitive opener 'To avoid the rush-hour traffic' must describe whoever avoids it, so 'Lena' must follow the comma. A train and a departure cannot avoid traffic, so 'an earlier train was taken by Lena,' 'the earlier train seemed wiser,' and 'an earlier departure made sense' all dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Carved from a single block of marble, [[the statue draws admiring crowds year-round]].
choices: NO CHANGE
people stand before the statue for hours
visitors admire the statue for hours
admiration for the statue runs deep
questions.explanation: 'Carved from a single block of marble' must modify the thing carved, the statue, so 'the statue' must follow the comma, and the original is correct. The other choices put 'visitors,' 'admiration,' or 'people' after the comma, none of which were carved from marble, so each dangles the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: The barista handed a muffin [[to the customer wrapped in wax paper]].
choices: NO CHANGE
to the wax-paper-wrapped customer
wrapped in wax paper to the customer
to the customer, who was wrapped in wax paper
questions.explanation: 'Wrapped in wax paper' describes the muffin, so it must sit beside 'muffin,' giving 'a muffin wrapped in wax paper to the customer.' 'To the customer wrapped in wax paper,' 'to the customer, who was wrapped in wax paper,' and 'to the wax-paper-wrapped customer' all wrap the customer instead of the muffin.

questions.questionText: Which choice most clearly limits the collected items to canned goods?
questions.stem: The volunteers [[only collected canned goods]] at the food drive, not clothing.
choices: NO CHANGE
only canned goods collected
collected only canned goods
collected canned goods at only
questions.explanation: 'Collected only canned goods' puts the limiter next to the items, making the contrast with clothing explicit. 'Only collected' can instead limit the action; 'only canned goods collected' has no appropriate main verb; and 'collected canned goods at only at the food drive' repeats the preposition and is malformed.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Painted bright yellow last spring, [[the old fence looked unfamiliar to Theo]].
choices: NO CHANGE
Theo barely recognized the old fence
recognizing the old fence proved hard
Theo walked past the old fence
questions.explanation: 'Painted bright yellow last spring' describes the fence, so 'the old fence' must follow the comma, and the original is correct. The other choices put 'Theo' or the gerund 'recognizing' after the comma, none of which was painted yellow, so each dangles the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Determined to finish the marathon, [[the last few miles tested Priscilla's resolve]].
choices: NO CHANGE
exhaustion set in near the end
the finish line stayed in sight
Priscilla pushed through the last few miles
questions.explanation: 'Determined to finish the marathon' describes the runner, so 'Priscilla' must follow the comma. Miles, a finish line, and exhaustion cannot feel determined, so 'the last few miles tested Priscilla's resolve,' 'the finish line stayed in sight,' and 'exhaustion set in near the end' all dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice most clearly indicates that the astrolabe, rather than the portrait, was made of brass?
questions.stem: The museum displayed the astrolabe [[beside a portrait that was made of brass]].
choices: NO CHANGE
that was made of brass beside a portrait
beside the brass-made portrait
beside a portrait, which was made of brass
questions.explanation: That was made of brass must directly follow astrolabe to identify the material of the instrument. Each other choice attaches brass to portrait. The correct position follows the intended referent specified by the question, not an assumption that only one object could ever be made of brass.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Wired with hundreds of sensors overnight, [[engineers monitored the bridge during the storm]].
choices: NO CHANGE
the monitoring continued all night
the bridge sent data to engineers during the storm
data flowed in throughout the storm
questions.explanation: 'Wired with hundreds of sensors overnight' must modify the thing wired, the bridge, so 'the bridge' must follow the comma. Engineers, data, and monitoring were not wired with sensors, so 'engineers monitored the bridge,' 'data flowed in,' and 'the monitoring continued' all dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: Painted by a teenage apprentice in 1620, [[historians now consider the portrait a masterpiece]].
choices: NO CHANGE
experts have studied it for years
the portrait is now considered a masterpiece
the museum guards it carefully
questions.explanation: 'Painted by a teenage apprentice in 1620' describes the portrait, so 'the portrait' must follow the comma. Historians, experts, and the museum were not painted in 1620, so those choices dangle the modifier.

questions.questionText: Which choice makes the sentence most grammatically acceptable?
questions.stem: To be considered for the fellowship, [[a research proposal must accompany each application]].
choices: NO CHANGE
the panel weighs each research proposal
each applicant must submit a research proposal
a research proposal is part of the requirements
questions.explanation: The infinitive opener 'To be considered for the fellowship' must describe whoever seeks consideration, so 'each applicant' must follow the comma. A proposal and the panel are not seeking the fellowship, so 'a research proposal must accompany each application,' 'a research proposal is part of the requirements,' and 'the panel weighs each research proposal' all dangle the modifier.

questions.stem: After being scanned at high resolution, [[the original letters were returned to their protective sleeves]].
questions.questionText: Which choice keeps the opening description attached to the object that was scanned?
choices: NO CHANGE
the archivists returned the original letters to their sleeves
returning the letters to their sleeves took the archivists an hour
protective sleeves once again held the original letters
questions.explanation: The original letters were scanned, and the keyed passive clause makes those letters its subject. The other choices make archivists, the activity of returning, or sleeves the subject, so the opener attaches to something that was not scanned. Passive voice is appropriate because the letters remain the topic.

questions.stem: The lab must inspect every seal before it releases a sample. To express that timing requirement clearly, the writer proposes: The lab [[only releases samples after inspection]].
questions.questionText: Which choice most clearly restricts when samples may be released?
choices: NO CHANGE
releases only samples after inspection
releases samples only after inspection
releases samples after only inspection
questions.explanation: Only after inspection explicitly restricts the time or condition of release. Only releases can limit the action; only samples restricts what is released. After only inspection is not idiomatic for the required timing relationship. All the samples must wait, so the limiter belongs with after inspection.
